carried_from.note: The column shows the panel's own number. It is carried across, not recomputed, so the two can never disagree.

verified.method: every published distance re-measured from the site coordinate to the stored foot of the perpendicular
verified.tolerance_basis: the source payload rounds distances to 3 dp of a km and feet to 6 dp of a degree; the tolerance is the sum of those two roundings, so this asserts agreement to the published precision and no further

bands.purpose: A screening band from measured geometry. It says how close the mapped network is, not whether a connection is obtainable.

beta.meaning: The measurement is published and checked. What it does not yet cover is stated below, so the number can be used for screening with its limits known.
not_covered: 11 kV, except an estimated UKPN layer; most sub-5 MW distribution connections are made at a voltage this column cannot see
the point of connection, which is not the site centroid the register supplies
connection queue position, curtailment and contracted capacity

caveat.distance: Straight-line distance to mapped geometry. Not a cable route, not a connection length, and no wayleave, crossing, terrain or consent content.
caveat.substation: A mapped substation point does not confirm capacity, voltage suitability, connection rights, queue position or acceptance by any network party.
caveat.coverage: Absence from a mapped layer is not absence on the ground.
caveat.headroom: Fault level and thermal headroom cannot be inferred from distance. They depend on DNO network data such as source impedance, fault infeed and existing committed connections, and are established by a connection study, not by geometry.

provenance.spine: DESNZ Renewable Energy Planning Database Q2 2026, OGL v3.0
provenance.network: OpenStreetMap via the pinned Ventus voltage layers, ODbL-1.0, (c) OpenStreetMap contributors

coverage.note: A project with no entry has no mapped circuit found, or no coordinate in the register. It is shown as a dash, never as a large number.
